content.text:
I found and fixed the bug, and `npm test` now passes (10 of 10). Against the old code the new tests fail with exactly the reported symptom: a ¥1,500 invoice charged as `150000`.

## Root cause
In `src/payments/gateway/payload.js`, the code turned the invoice currency into the gateway's lower-case form (`'JPY'` becomes `'jpy'`) before working out the amount to charge:

```js
const currency = toGatewayCurrency(invoice.currency);   // 'jpy'
amount: toMinor(invoice.total, currency),               // looks up 'jpy'
```

To convert an amount to the gateway's smallest unit (cents, yen), `toMinor` looks up how many decimal places the currency uses. That lookup table in `src/lib/currency/registry.js` only has upper-case codes. `'jpy'` wasn't found, so it silently used the default of 2 decimals and multiplied by 100. Yen and won have no decimals, so ¥1,500 became 150,000.

The PDF was correct because the invoice code uses the upper-case `'JPY'`. US and EU customers were unaffected because USD and EUR really do use 2 decimals, so the wrong default happened to give the right answer.

It's also wrong in the other direction for currencies with 3 decimals: a BHD 12.345 invoice was charged as 1235 fils instead of 12345, about 10× too little. VND and CLP were overcharged 100× like yen and won.

## Fix
- **`src/payments/gateway/payload.js`**: the amount is now calculated from the invoice's own upper-case code. Only the `currency` field sent to the gateway is lower-cased.
- **`src/lib/currency/registry.js`**: the lookups now ignore case, so a lower-case code from any caller finds the right currency instead of falling back to the 2-decimal default.

## Regression tests (`test/charge.test.js`)
- JPY ¥1,500 is charged as `1500`, with currency `'jpy'`.
- KRW ₩25,000 is charged as `25000`.
- BHD 12.345 is charged as `12345` (the 3-decimal case).
- `toMinor(1500, 'jpy')` and `toMinor(1500, 'JPY')` both return `1500`.

Separately, JPY, KRW, VND and CLP customers charged since this bug went in were overcharged and probably need refunds. BHD and KWD customers were undercharged. You can find the affected charges in the `invoice.charged` audit events, whose `amount` field holds the inflated value. I haven't committed anything.
